lines.en: A familiar man opens the door to a familiar limousine and I crawl into the back next to Tsubasa.
And while I’m no stranger to immediately departing the residence of a woman after ejaculating into her mouth, it’s not exactly common for the red carpet to be rolled out for my walk of shame.
This, combined with the fact that I’m now quite literally trapped in the back of a moving vehicle with the closest thing I know to a super-villain, is a bit disconcerting to say the least.
I doubt this car will be driving off a cliff anytime soon, though. Not with precious cargo tucked safely into the backseat.
But should that precious cargo need to lighten the load, I’m sure I’ll be the first to go.
I just hope these hands of stone will be enough to protect the wooden heart I hide behind my glass ribs once I’m forced to dance with the pavement at roughly fifty miles per hour.
: You’re not always this nervous in moving cars...are you, Akira? Can I assume that you’re once again seeing me as something far more scary than I truly am?
: I’m always this nervous. So I’m sorry, but you won’t be able to take the credit for my mannerisms this time.
: At least not all of it. You’re definitely adding to everything, though.
: If it helps to dispel your worries, I can assure you Ishimoto is an excellent driver. He’s been chauffeuring me for many years now. You’re in the best of hands, I promise.
: I believe you. The present can’t change the past, though.
: It can change the way you perceive it.
: We all look differently when we’re hit by the light in certain ways.
: For example, you look much more handsome now than you did under that drab bar’s red glow. I suppose it helps that you’re not currently being fellated, though.
: You literally watched the entire time.
: I looked away on several occasions. Never for long. But I won’t sit here and let you blame me for being once more entranced by just how many women you’re willing to conquer.
: Aren’t you the same girl who told me she’s used to watching women being sold off like cattle?
: I am. But I can’t say I have much experience with...farmers, so to speak.
: I wasn’t just conquering Sara. I genuinely care about her.
: Do you genuinely care about me?
: Not really.
: Hahah! Not yet, you mean.
: We simply just haven’t had enough time to get to know one another yet.
: You’re the mystery here. I’m convinced you know practically all there is to know about me now that you have my full name.
: Have I not already told you a great deal about myself? We’ve gone over my family’s history...how I came to be involved with the Tsukioka family...you even know where I went to high school.
: What more would you like to inquire about?
: What you want with me.
: I’ve told you that on several occasions as well. You’re an...asset. But you’re also a friend.
: It doesn’t always feel that way, though.
: Yes, well...
: I have to maintain a certain...distance, you see.
: If we become too friendly, someone may notice. And I have a reputation to uphold.
: I believed that right up until you started stroking Sara’s hair while she was fellating me.
: I’m speaking primarily about what goes on within the manor. You know that the vast majority of my time is spent within its grounds, Akira.
: The world outside of my walls is hardly even real as far as I’m concerned.
: Yeah, I kind of figured that’s why you showed no qualms when it came to subtly belittling Sara in her own business.
: You really do care about her, don’t you? You seem awfully offended by some of my dialogue choices tonight.
: She has feelings, Tsubasa.
: And you think a few measly jabs at her status put her in greater jeopardy than the fact that you’re on the brink of leading two teenage girls into a debauched life of sex disguised as love?
: If it is only two, of course. You could be involved with your entire class for all I know.
: I imagine you already would know.
: Perhaps I do and I’m just keeping it a secret until I encounter you with them next. Regardless, you stand to hurt her far more than I ever could.
: So maybe it would be wise to not treat me like the bad guy when you’re the one traipsing all over Kumon-mi, sowing seeds of destruction in every single place you roam.
: What’s wrong, Aki-kun? Cat got your tongue?
: Never call me that again. Do you understand?
: No. Could you say it a little louder, please? Maybe grab my shoulders and shake me around a bit?
: And have your driver pull over and beat me to death? Pass. Just...don’t call me that. Please.
: You really are interesting, Akira. You remind me a lot of an old friend when you get passionate like that.
: It’s not passion. It’s anger and resentment and fear and sadness and-
: And all of those things can combine to form passion under the right circumstances. It’s like I said before. Everything changes with the light. Neither you nor I are exceptions to that.
Tsubasa reaches forward, tracing circles around my knee with the tip of her index finger. But there doesn’t seem to be any...intent to it.
In fact, I’m not even sure if she’s aware she’s doing it. I imagine she is as it’s hard for me to think anything she does isn’t cleverly calculated, but still.
It makes me comfortable and scared at the same time. But I can’t figure out how to make those things combine. Which makes what she said just seconds ago even harder to understand.
: Tsubasa...what do you think you’d be doing right now if you never met me?
: Why, sipping some of the poorest wine that’s ever touched my tongue, of course.
: Not just tonight, but...in general.
: Both of your daughters were struggling to learn how the “outside world” functioned or whatever. And you didn’t have anyone’s backstory to start prying open as your newest hobby.
: If we never crossed paths at that onsen however many years ago it was, everything would be different right now.
: Is that really what you believe?
: I mean...yeah. That was the catalyst that ultimately brought Touka into my life. And without Touka, we’d have no reason to see each other at all.
: I suppose we wouldn’t, would we?
: But I’m not sure it would even matter, if you’d like my honest opinion.
: Fate has a funny way of forcing things together. And I truly believe that our paths were meant to cross one way or the other.
: And why is that? Because you’re not important to me and I’m not important to you. What would fate have to do with any of this?
: ...Tsubasa?
: Forgive me, Akira. I’ve said too much. So I’m going to go ahead and drop this subject now.
: ...What?
: But as a consolation prize, I’ll allow you to choose our next conversation topic.
: I’d like to talk more about fate please.
: Ha ha. Very funny. But no. I was thinking something more...fun. Personal, even.
: Sure. But be aware that you’ll have to do all of the heavy lifting since I’m not good at talking about that kind of stuff.
: That’s fine. I probably know it all already anyway.
: Ha ha. Very funny.
: Any suggestions? Things you’ve been dying to know more about? My three sizes? My...ideal partner?
: Careful, Tsubasa. Ishimoto might relay anything you say about your ideal partner to your husband.
: Ishimoto will do nothing of the sort as he understands he’d be castrated for it. Isn’t that correct, Ishimoto?
: Of course, madam. Your word is law.
: Ahh, how I love being rich.
: Well, at the risk of finding out your ideal partner would be anything or anyone other than me, how about this-
: What’s the craziest thing you’ve ever done?
: The craziest thing I’ve ever done?
: I suppose it would have to be giving you my youngest daughter’s phone number. That could have gone south in many ways. But you’ve yet to disappoint me in response, Akira. I’m proud.
: I meant sexually.
: Sexually?
: If you’re going to encroach on my sex life and watch my friends go down on me, the least you can do is give me something to hold over you as well.
: I don’t intend to hold anything over you, Akira. I was merely enjoying a little show. Besides, isn’t it rather daring to ask a woman of my caliber about her sexual history?
: You said I could choose. This is what I’m choosing. It’s either this or we go back to talking about fate and how you’re, once again, weirdly hiding seemingly relevant information from me.
: The craziest thing I’ve ever done?
: Has there even been anything like that?
: I hope. A life of nothing but consensual sex in the missionary position with your husband sounds extremely boring and unfulfilling.
: And I can confirm that it is.
: Though, there was that one time when I had intercourse with four members of the massage staff at once.
: Sorry. Did I hear that correctly just now?
: I’m not sure. What did you hear?
: That you had sex with four guys at once?
: Oh, yes. The night before I was married. It’s a family tradition.
: To get fucked by four guys at once the night before your wedding???
: Why do you sound so perplexed by this extremely common ritual?
: Because that’s not a common ritual at all?? And it paints you in a completely different light now that I know you’re getting gang-banged by masseurs.
: Well, how many men do lower and middle class women typically bed before the night of their wedding?
: Probably none? Maybe their fiancée?
: Well, that sounds rather boring too, doesn’t it?
: Besides, I’m not being gang-banged by anyone. At least not on a consistent basis. That was decades ago.
: And while there’s still a full staff of therapists on call at Tsukioka Manor, none of them would dare touch me in such a way even if I commanded them to. Trust me, I’ve tried.
: Then how are you-
: I’m not. It’s as simple as that.
: I have little time for such pleasures anymore in the first place. So please forgive me if I...crossed any lines tonight.
: It was nice living vicariously through someone else for a change. I don’t often want to do that.
: I’ll admit that watching you dominate Chika was far more pleasurable, though. The taboo factor added a layer of depravity that, while initially shameful, was quite invigorating in hindsight.
: So you and your husband just...
: I see you more than him at this point. He and I don’t even sleep in the same room anymore.
: Why not?
: That’s just the way things worked out, I suppose.
: And apart from him and the massage staff, I barely have any experience with anyone at all.
: Though, there was that one time when my friends and I ran off to the urban district and I had intercourse with four men I’d met at a party.
: Jesus Christ, Tsubasa.
: No, I don’t think he was there. I may be old, but I’m not that old.
: Why is it always four?
: Because once you start adding more than that, no one knows what to do.
: So what I’m learning is you have a ton of experience and you’re just once again tricking me into looking at you in a certain light.
: Perhaps. But by that logic, wouldn’t you say it’s possible neither of those...what do you call them — orgies — happened at all, is it not?
: I...guess? But why would you want me to think you’re experienced when you’re not?
: Why indeed?
: I really hate when you answer questions by just...questioning the question. It’s impossible to learn anything that way.
: That’s the point, Akira.
: Madam, we’ll be arriving at Master Arakawa’s residence in approximately one minute. If you have yet to finish conversing, I can circle the area or-
: No, you may proceed to the destination. Master Arakawa and I are done here.
: We are? Because it sounded like things were finally getting good. I’m actually not intimidated for once.
: Are you coming onto me, Akira?
Her fingers stops tracing circles on my knee. It slides further up my leg instead.
: I’m a married woman, you know...and based on the girls I’ve seen you with, I think it’s safe to say I’m...not your type.
I grab her wrist. She doesn’t flinch.
: I’m not afraid of you, Tsubasa.
: Not anymore, you’re not...
: But that’s because I spoon-fed you certain details that shattered the illusion.
: That...wait, what?
: It’s rather funny how quickly a powerful woman can be seen as weak once certain...details come out.
: All it took for you to change the way you look at me was a little bit of lust and some seductive whispers — tall tales of times that I’ve been vulnerable.
: Why is it that being swallowed up by the pleasures of the flesh makes you seem stronger — but me seem weak?
: I’m as scary as I’ve always been. You’re just easy to manipulate.
: Uhh...so, wait. None of that ever happened? I’m confused.
: It all changes with the light, Akira.
: Sometimes, the things you see aren’t really there.
: And other times, there’s something you can’t help but miss.
: Madam, we’ve arrived.
: Maybe it’s because you’re distracted...maybe you just don’t want to see it...
: But you can never know what’s real until you experience it.
She swats my hand away and leans back in her seat.
: And some things are harder to experience than they look.
The driver opens my door and steps to the side.
: Goodnight, Akira.
: It’s been a...pleasure.
She winks at me once more.
The door to the limo closes.
And I go back to my room.
I don’t think I’ll ever understand her.
Tsubasa’s affection has increased to [tsubasa_love]!
